summary.en: Israel has expanded road networks and opened new bases in southern Lebanon while conducting airstrikes on Qantara and overflights that injured a Lebanese footballer and led to the detention of a 65‑year-old retired engineer. Hezbollah arrested five members in Batroun, continued artillery fire on Israeli positions, and began cash payments to war victims and displaced families. Former Iraqi MP Ahmed al-Alwani was killed in Beirut, prompting further updates. France opened a probe into alleged Israeli war crimes and protests against Israeli attacks occurred in Sweden. The conflict caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israel har utvidet veinettet og åpnet nye baser i sørlige Libanon mens de gjennomførte luftangrep mot Qantara og overflyvninger som skadet en libanesisk fotballspiller og førte til fengsling av en 65‑år gammel pensjonert ingeniør. Hezbollah arresterte fem medlemmer i Batroun, fortsatte artilleriskudd mot israelske posisjoner, og begynte å betale kontantstøtte til krigsofre og fordrevede familier. Den tidligere irakiske stortingsrepresentanten Ahmed al-Alwani ble drept i Beirut, noe som førte til ytterligere oppdateringer. Frankrike åpnet en etterforskning av påståtte israelske krigsforbrytelser og protester mot israelske angrep fant sted i Sverige. Konflikten forårsaket 4 335 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
